'''Simona Gabriela Kossak''' ({{Date range|1943|May|30|2007|March|15|df=y}}) was a Polish [[biologist]], [[ecologist]], and professor of forest sciences. Kossak is known for her efforts to preserve the remnants of natural [[ecosystems]] in [[Poland]]. Her work dealt with, among other things, the [[behavioral ecology]] of [[mammals]]. She sometimes referred to herself as a "zoo-psychologist."<ref>[https://culture.pl/en/article/the-extraordinary-life-of-simona-kossak Janusz R. Kowalczyk: The Extraordinary Life of Simona Kossak] 22 July 2015, ''culture.pl'', accessed 3 September 2021</ref>

== Early life ==
Kossak was born in [[Kraków]], during the [[Second World War]], when the city was [[General Government|occupied]] by German forces.<ref>[http://www.encyklopedia.puszcza-bialowieska.eu/index.php?dzial=haslo&id=27 Kossak Simona, prof. dr hab.(1943-2007)] ''Encyklopedia - Puszcza Białoweiska'', accessed 6 September 2021</ref>

== Career ==
She achieved a BSc and MSc in Biology in 1976. In 1980, the Scientific Council of the Forest Research Institute awarded Kossak with a doctoral degree in Forest Sciences on the basis of her doctoral dissertation ''Research on the trophic situation of roe deer in the habitat of fresh mixed coniferous forest in the [[Białowieża Forest|Białowieża Primeval Forest]]'' and, in 1991, with a postdoctoral degree in Forest Sciences on the basis of her postdoctoral dissertation ''Environmental and intraspecific determinants of the feeding behavior of roe deer ([[Capreolus capreolus]] L.) in the forest environment''.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20070825165910/http://www.ibles.waw.pl/struktura/zln/pracownicy/skossak.htm Prof. dr hab. Simona Kossak] ''web.archive.org'', accessed 4 September 2021</ref> In 1997, she received the academic title of Professor of Forest Sciences.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20070825165910/http://www.ibles.waw.pl/struktura/zln/pracownicy/skossak.htm Prof. dr hab. Simona Kossak] ''web.archive.org'', accessed 4 September 2021</ref>

Kossak worked at the Mammal Research Institute of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]] in [[Białowieża]] and at the Forest Research Institute at the Department of Natural Forests, where she was the director from January 2003 until her death in 2007.<ref>[http://www.encyklopedia.puszcza-bialowieska.eu/index.php?dzial=haslo&id=27 Kossak Simona, prof. dr hab.(1943-2007)] ''Encyklopedia - Puszcza Białoweiska'', accessed 4 September 2021</ref> She was also one of the originators of the UOZ-1 repeller, a device that warns wild animals of passing trains.<ref>{{Cite web| title=Polak potrafi {{!}} wynalazek {{!}} Uwaga, pociag! | language=pl | trans-title=A Pole can {{!}} invent {{!}} Watch out, train! | url=https://neel.com.pl/web/pliki/publikacje/GW_2015.09.08.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160425053142/http://www.neel.com.pl/web/pliki/publikacje/GW_2015.09.08.pdf | archive-date=2016-04-25}}</ref> In October 2000, Kossak was awarded the [[Golden Cross of Merit]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20070825165910/http://www.ibles.waw.pl/struktura/zln/pracownicy/skossak.htm Prof. dr hab. Simona Kossak] ''web.archive.org'', accessed 4 September 2021</ref>

Kossak was known for her uncompromising views about and actions for the protection of nature, especially in the Białowieża Forest, where she lived in the old forester's lodge "Dziedzinka" for over 30 years.<ref>[https://culture.pl/en/article/the-extraordinary-life-of-simona-kossak Janusz R. Kowalczyk: The Extraordinary Life of Simona Kossak] 22 July 2015, ''culture.pl'', accessed 3 September 2021</ref><ref>[https://przekroj.pl/en/culture/a-paradise-called-dziedzinka-zbigniew-swiech A Paradise Called Dziedzinka: The Lodge in the Białowieża Forest] 1974, ''przekroj.pl'', accessed 4 September 2021</ref>

== Personal life ==
Kossak came from a well-known artistic family. She was the daughter of [[Jerzy Kossak]], sister of [[Gloria Kossak]], granddaughter of [[Wojciech Kossak]], and great-granddaughter of [[Juliusz Kossak]], and niece of [[Magdalena Samozwaniec]] and [[Maria Pawlikowska-Jasnorzewska]].<ref>[https://culture.pl/en/article/the-extraordinary-life-of-simona-kossak Janusz R. Kowalczyk: The Extraordinary Life of Simona Kossak] 22 July 2015, ''culture.pl'', accessed 3 September 2021</ref> Lech Wilczek, a naturalist, photographer, and writer, was Kossak's lifelong partner.<ref>[https://culture.pl/en/article/the-extraordinary-life-of-simona-kossak Janusz R. Kowalczyk: The Extraordinary Life of Simona Kossak] 22 July 2015, ''culture.pl'', accessed 3 September 2021</ref><ref>[https://polandin.com/40619305/distinguished-photographer-of-nature-dies-at-88 Distinguished photographer of nature dies at 88] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210904164338/https://polandin.com/40619305/distinguished-photographer-of-nature-dies-at-88 |date=2021-09-04 }} 28 December 2018, ''polandin.com'', accessed 4 September 2021</ref>

== Legacy ==
In 2024, Kossak's life was the subject of a [[Biographical film|biographical]] [[Drama (film and television)|drama film]] directed and written by Adrian Panek. The film stars [[Sandra Drzymalska]] as the main protagonist and premiered at the 24th [[New Horizons Film Festival|New Horizons International Film Festival]] in July 2024.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vogue.pl/a/recenzja-filmu-simona-kossak-z-sandra-drzymalska-i-jakubem-gierszalem-w-rolach-glownych|title=Film "Simona Kossak" o słynnej badaczce z Sandrą Drzymalską pozostawia uczucie niedosytu|first=Vogue|last=Polska|date=July 23, 2024|website=Vogue Polska}}</ref>

* Kossak, S. (1992). Foraging habits and behaviour of moose calves in virgin forest. ''Acta Theriologica'', 37, 51-51.
